value.loc: Abstract, p.1; Sec. 2 Agreement and Other Election Indices; Sec. 3
value.quote: We consider the notions of agreement, diversity, and polarization in ordinal elections
value.note: The main object is a set of election indices: functions mapping a preference profile to a real number that measures agreement, diversity or polarization. k-Kemeny is used only to compute distances for these indices, not as a rule producing a collective decision. No strategic aspects are studied. This is a measurement and diagnostics paper, not a study of a voting procedure.

C0.reason: The paper studies descriptive indices of preference profiles and their computation rather than a procedure aggregating inputs into a collective decision, so INELIG fits better and the doubt rule does not apply.
